# Results — Study 601 (Factor ETFs — Live Test)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
iShares factor ETFs (USMV min-vol, MTUM momentum, VLUE value, QUAL quality) promised academic
factor exposure in a one-ticket wrapper; a decade-plus later, did each deliver?** — audited on
the LIVE products' monthly total returns vs SPY since each fund's inception. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-07-03**; monthly stats sliced to **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `fd36c691c5cb`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily auto-adjusted closes (**total-return**, i.e. **net of each fund's 0.15%/yr fee**) — SPY, USMV, MTUM, VLUE, QUAL + style proxies (IWD/IWF, SPHQ, 9 SPDR sectors) + ^IRX rf |
| Windows | USMV 2011-11 → 2026-06 (**176** months); MTUM & VLUE 2013-05 → 2026-06 (**158**); QUAL 2013-08 → 2026-06 (**155**) |
| Risk-free | ^IRX 13-week T-bill discount yield, prior month-end level (known in advance — no look-ahead) |
| Execution / costs | the funds are **buy-and-hold products** — no trading rule is executed in this study; the only constructed signal (the sector 12-1 WML proxy) is formed on months *t−12…t−2*, known at the **end of month *t−1*** and applied to month *t* — exactly **one** month of lag; buying a wrapper costs one ~1–2 bps spread, no shorts anywhere |

> **Selection / survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** These four are the flagship
> iShares factor funds — the biggest **survivors** of the 2010s smart-beta launch wave (dozens
> of competitor factor ETFs closed). Auditing the four largest live wrappers likely flatters
> the *average* factor-ETF experience; it is the right panel only for the question asked —
> "did the flagship products deliver?". The SPHQ quality proxy carries its own caveat: SPHQ
> switched to the S&P 500 Quality index in 2016, so its pre-2016 spread reflects an older
> quality methodology.

## Axis 1 — EXPOSURE delivery: every wrapper carries its stated style (*t* ≥ 7.4)

USMV's promise is mechanical (a lower-risk profile); the other three must load on their
style's **realized long-short spread** (two-factor NW regression: fund excess on [SPY excess,
spread]) and out-run SPY in the months their factor won (Welch *t* + a 10,000-draw
same-density random-calendar placebo).

| fund | stated-style test | delivery statistic | spread-sign split (active, factor-won vs factor-lost) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **USMV** | beta < 1, lower vol | beta **0.689**, ***t*(β<1) = −7.52**; vol ratio **0.799** CI [0.741, 0.876] → **~20% less vol** (CI 12–26%), at the low edge of the promised 20–30% | — (mechanical) |
| **MTUM** | sector 12-1 WML loading | **+0.326**, NW ***t* = +7.45** (R² 81.9%) | **+96.2** vs **−64.5** bps/mo — diff +160.7 bps, Welch *t* **+4.59**, placebo *p* < 0.0001 |
| **VLUE** | IWD−IWF value-spread loading | **+0.517**, NW ***t* = +9.99** (R² 85.6%) | **+131.2** vs **−84.5** bps/mo — diff +215.7 bps, Welch *t* **+6.06**, placebo *p* < 0.0001 |
| **QUAL** | SPHQ−SPY quality-spread loading | **+0.384**, NW ***t* = +8.76** (R² 97.4%) | **+20.7** vs **−26.4** bps/mo — diff +47.1 bps, Welch *t* **+3.63**, placebo *p* = 0.0003 |

Every product **delivers the exposure it printed on the label**, at *t*-statistics between
7.4 and 10 on the real tape. This half of the pitch is decisively REAL.

## Axis 2 — ALPHA delivery: none (all |*t*| ≤ 1.24, robust to NW lags 3/6/12)

| fund | CAPM alpha | NW *t* (lags 3) | NW *t* (lags 6) | NW *t* (lags 12) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| USMV | +0.69%/yr | +0.45 | +0.47 | +0.47 |
| MTUM | +2.65%/yr | +1.11 | +1.10 | +1.24 |
| VLUE | −0.96%/yr | −0.36 | −0.32 | −0.31 |
| QUAL | −0.23%/yr | −0.29 | −0.28 | −0.27 |

The factor literature promised risk-adjusted **alpha**; the live wrappers show none. Alphas
sit between −1.0% and +2.7%/yr with every *t* far below 2 at every lag choice. USMV's positive
Sharpe-flattering profile nets out to +0.69%/yr of CAPM alpha (*t* 0.47) — the risk *profile*
delivered, the risk-adjusted *premium* did not certify.

## Axis 3 — did ANY beat SPY outright? (same-window races, all net of fees)

| fund | CAGR gap vs SPY | Sharpe vs SPY | active mean (NW *t*) |
|---|--:|---|---|
| USMV | **−3.50 pp/yr** | 0.887 vs 0.959 | −28.9 bps/mo (*t* −1.94) |
| MTUM | **+2.42 pp/yr** | 0.934 vs 0.887 | +19.9 bps/mo (*t* +0.93) |
| VLUE | −0.57 pp/yr | 0.722 vs 0.887 | +0.2 bps/mo (*t* +0.01) |
| QUAL | −0.39 pp/yr | 0.834 vs 0.867 | −2.7 bps/mo (*t* −0.41) |

**No fund beat SPY at any statistical significance.** Three of four lagged on CAGR; only MTUM
finished ahead (+2.42 pp/yr) and even that reads *t* = 0.93 — noise. USMV, the biggest factor
ETF on earth, trailed by 3.5 pp/yr (that's what beta 0.69 does in a 15-year bull tape) — its
*Sharpe* is nearly SPY's, which is precisely the min-vol proposition, but the outright race is
lost. **Busted.**

## Style-proxy sanity (the regressors themselves)

| proxy | window | mean | NW *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| sector 12-1 WML (top3−bottom3, 1-mo lag) | 2000-01 → 2026-06 | +5.5 bps/mo (13.9%/yr vol) | +0.28 |
| IWD−IWF (value − growth) | 2000-06 → 2026-06 | −4.4 bps/mo | −0.22 |
| SPHQ−SPY (quality − market) | 2006-01 → 2026-06 | −4.8 bps/mo | −0.42 |

The style spreads themselves earned ~nothing over the window — the funds faithfully tracked
factors that didn't pay. Exposure delivery and premium delivery are different promises.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful

Deterministic joint (market, spread, fund) monthly world, 168 months, planted beta / loading /
alpha (`data.synthetic_world`):

| world | beta (t vs 1) | loading (NW *t*) | alpha (NW *t*) |
|---|---|---|---|
| null (β=1, s=0, α=0) | 1.019 (+1.82) | +0.010 (+0.56) | −0.56%/yr (−1.02) |
| planted (β=0.7, s=0.5, α=+3%) | 0.717 (**−10.54**) | +0.510 (**+27.37**) | +2.44%/yr (**+4.43**) |

The estimators stay quiet on the null and recover every planted parameter. *(Machinery proof
only — never cited in support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL (exposure delivery).** Every wrapper demonstrably carries its stated style
  on the live tape: USMV beta 0.689 (*t* vs 1 = **−7.52**), vol ratio 0.80 (CI 0.74–0.88);
  MTUM WML loading *t* = **+7.45**; VLUE value loading *t* = **+9.99**; QUAL quality loading
  *t* = **+8.76**, all with spread-sign splits at Welch *t* 3.6–6.1 and placebo *p* ≤ 0.0003.
  Carries the flagship-survivor selection caveat (these are the four biggest *surviving*
  factor ETFs of the launch wave).
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The exposure is genuinely buyable — 0.15%/yr, penny spreads,
  tens of billions of AUM, one ticket. But the thing the exposure was sold to harvest — factor
  **alpha** — did not show up: CAPM alphas −1.0% to +2.7%/yr, all |*t*| ≤ 1.24, and the style
  spreads themselves paid ~zero over the live window. What you can buy is a risk *profile*
  (USMV: −20% vol, down-capture 66%), not an edge. A real, deliverable product wrapped around
  a premium that hasn't paid — Fragile, not Investable.
- **"Did any beat SPY outright?" — BUSTED.** None at significance. Three of four lagged on
  CAGR; MTUM's +2.42 pp/yr reads *t* = 0.93. The decade-plus live test says: the wrappers
  delivered the factors, the factors didn't deliver the market-beating.
